_about: Completed-print lines that need no facts at all: the last resort that always fits.
_license: Original to Print Handy; MIT with the project.
entries: Another successful print, another shelf quietly wondering where its free space went.
The printer did the work, but someone here will absolutely take the credit.
Somewhere, a store-bought version is feeling deeply disrespected right now.
Congratulations, your robot butler has completed another very important plastic errand.
That sound you hear is a spool getting lighter and confidence getting louder.
Finished, flawless, and already being photographed like a newborn with better layer lines.
You watched a machine melt plastic for hours and called it supervision, respectfully.
The hobby promised one small print and somehow delivered a whole lifestyle.
Proof that patience, electricity, and stubbornness can become a physical object.
Another masterpiece enters the collection, population growing, storage plan still pending.
The printer has finished, so the human may now resume pretending to relax.
Hours of humming, moments of checking, and seconds of triumph complete the ritual.
A triumph of engineering, assuming triumph includes checking the camera every ten minutes.
Some collect art, some collect stamps, and some manufacture their own clutter proudly.
Done at last, with not a single dramatic bed peel, which feels suspiciously professional.
The filament is gone, the object is real, and the excuse budget is empty.
Behold, the result of saying just one more print with a straight face.
Another object joins the household, and the shelf negotiations begin anew.
Slow, steady, and successful: basically a turtle with a heating element and fans.
The machine printed, the human hovered, and together they call that teamwork.
Victory is sweet, smells faintly of warm plastic, and needs a place to sit.
Completed without drama, which for this hobby counts as a special occasion.
Your future self thanks you for making this instead of buying it in minutes.
A whole print finished, and only minimal staring through a camera was required.
The bed is cooling, the part is perfect, and someone is already planning another.
Imagine explaining this hobby to aliens: we melt string into shapes for joy.
Another layer-by-layer magic trick, performed extremely slowly by a very patient box.
Finished successfully, which means the next print will be twice as ambitious, naturally.
The spool lost some weight, the desk gained some glory, and everyone wins here.
This is what peak productivity looks like when productivity wears a plastic costume.
Done, dusted, and admired from at least four angles for quality assurance purposes.
The printer rested its motors while the human immediately opened another model tab.
A successful print today keeps the just-buy-it comments away, but only barely.
Somewhere a designer uploaded a file, and this household turned it into homework.
Warm plastic, cool result, and a human pretending this was all effortless.
Another finish line crossed at a pace that would embarrass a glacier, beautifully.
The collection grows, the storage bins multiply, and nobody learns a single thing.
Completed: one object, zero shortcuts, and several hours of premium robot humming.
You did not just print a thing; you scheduled joy several hours in advance.
The machine has delivered, and the human has already forgotten the waiting part.
Success tastes like victory and looks like it needs a tiny display stand.
Another print, another reason the craft store thinks you live there now.
Finished cleanly, which is the printer showing off and honestly earning it.
The art of turning electricity and string into shelf decorations continues undefeated.
Hours invested, object acquired, and the phrase useful hobby defended once again.
A robot made this slowly so a human could feel accomplished quickly.
The print is done, the camera can rest, and the hovering may officially end.
Done and looking sharp enough to make the calibration cubes quietly jealous.
Plastic has been promoted to product, pending approval from the nearest shelf.
Another successful session of a human watching a robot do crafts, applauding softly.
The finish is so clean that even the first layer is bragging quietly.
This hobby runs on patience, plastic, and pretending the storage problem is solved.
Completed beautifully, proving that slow and steady occasionally wins the entire race.
A new object has arrived, and it brought its own photo shoot with it.
The printer clocked out proudly while the human started a victory lap indoors.
Some chase trophies; this household manufactures them one layer at a time.
Finished at last: the waiting was long, the hovering was longer, the smile longest.
Another day, another object that definitely needed to exist, according to local sources.
The spool is lighter, the desk is fuller, and the cycle remains gloriously unbroken.
Success again, which can only mean the next project just got more ambitious.
